public_rationale: Marcus said nobody 'even pretends anymore' to be close to intervention-free driving off the Interstate. In January 2022, Reuters quoted Musk saying he would be 'shocked' if Tesla did not achieve full self-driving safer than a human that year. In October 2022, three months before the post, he again promoted FSD on general roads with 'very few, if any, interventions.' So the most prominent figure in the paragraph was still claiming to be close. That contradicts the plain reading of 'nobody pretends.' The verdict depends on this reading. Marcus's broader point, that no such drive had happened, is consistent with the evidence.
limitations: The claim is hyperbolic. A reader who takes 'doing that' to mean only the specific LA-to-NYC drive could see it differently.
Musk's statements come from news reports, not a primary transcript.
Part of e2 is the reporter's paraphrase.

public_payload.normalized_proposition: Highway miles are the easy part of the promised intervention-free LA-to-NYC drive, and nobody even pretends anymore to be close to making such a drive off the Interstate.

statement.excerpt: (And highways miles are the easy part; nobody even pretends anymore to be close to doing that off the Interstate).

from_speaker: highways miles are the easy part
to be close to doing that
'that' = an intervention-free drive, without human assistance, from LA to NYC
our_interpretation: Plain reading: as of the post, no prominent self-driving developer was publicly claiming to be close to fully hands-off, intervention-free driving on ordinary non-highway roads, of the kind a cross-country drive off the Interstate would need.
He named no period. 'Anymore' points to the recent state at the time of the post, so I use roughly the year before the post (2022-01-01 to 2023-01-18).
Public claims by Tesla's CEO about full self-driving on all roads count as someone 'pretending to be close', because the paragraph is about Musk's promises.
The side remark that highway miles are 'the easy part' is treated as framing. It is widely accepted and not the testable core.
criteria.support_condition: In the year before the post, no major developer or its leadership publicly claimed to be near general, intervention-free autonomous driving on non-highway roads.
criteria.contradiction_condition: In that period, a major developer's leadership publicly claimed to be close to full self-driving with few or no interventions on general roads, including city streets.

evidence.excerpt: “I would be shocked if we do not achieve full self-driving safer than human this year. I would be shocked,” Musk said
evidence.explanation: Within the year before the post, Tesla's CEO publicly said full self-driving on general roads was imminent. That is someone 'pretending' to be close to off-highway autonomy.

evidence.excerpt: Musk reiterated during the conference that he still believes Tesla can achieve full self-driving. The FSD software should be able to provide customers with a generally hands-free solution for driving, with very few, if any, interventions from the drivers.
evidence.explanation: Three months before the post, Musk was still promoting near-intervention-free FSD on general roads. Part of this sentence is the reporter's paraphrase.

evidence.excerpt: the wide rollout of the FSD Beta program does not equal FSD getting out of Beta and becoming the autonomous driving feature that Musk has promised for many years.
evidence.explanation: Shows the claims were promises, not achievements. This fits Marcus's wider point but not the 'nobody pretends' wording.
